dedupe_keys.name: digital earth australia dea with dea maps and the dea knowledge hub

description: Digital Earth Australia, run by Geoscience Australia, corrects, curates and makes freely available decades of satellite imagery of Australian landscapes, with analysis-ready imagery and derived datasets that can be downloaded, accessed through web services, and viewed on the interactive DEA Maps. Its Knowledge Hub catalogues the data products by theme (baseline satellite data, land and vegetation, inland water, sea, ocean and coast, hazards, and external data), with user guides, DEA Notebooks that show how to analyse the data in Python with the DEA Tools package, and validation reports comparing analysis-ready data with field measurements. The data is managed with the Open Data Cube. DEA serves environment, agriculture, government and emergency management users, the last for monitoring and responding to fire, flood and other natural hazards. The archive is described as free and open-source, and each product page in the catalogue gives ways to access the data. Caveats: DEA Maps is rendered by scripts, and releases and outages are announced as technical alerts. Coverage is Australia. It supports hazard exposure analysis, for example flood and fire extents near infrastructure, and land and water monitoring; related records are the DLR EOC Geoservice and ESA Earth Online.
